# Local Projects

A WhaleIsle Project links one existing local directory to one lasting coordinator conversation. Add Project from the new-conversation directory menu and choose a directory. Repeating the same canonical directory opens its original Project and coordinator. Non-Git directories work without initialization. Creation starts no model and creates no worker or branch. Its coordinator is the native Team Lead. The Project category also exposes the same add action.

The main surface remains the native conversation, composer and model controls. Ask questions, request work, add conditions and stop work there. The coordinator directly answers questions supported by known facts or existing results and delegates actual work to continuing workers. Workstream IDs stay internal; follow-up uses the original worker Session, cwd and history. Worker processes and files run locally; model requests use the configured provider.

## Runtime

`project-coordinator` exposes `project_request`, `project_read_store`, `project_delegate`, `project_deliver`, `project_stop` and scoped native Team reads. Its cwd is `$DSH_HOME/projects/<projectId>`, distinct from the directory displayed as the Project’s work object. Existing `session/presentation.owner = 'project'` supplies display ownership. The coordinator keeps a normal editable composer and is not attached as a member of the code Workspace.

Each worker uses the independent `project-worker` preset and the existing fresh, continuable `spawn` provider. A caller-reserved childId is persisted before native creation. Existing workers receive assignments through the native Team mailbox; an absent or damaged original Session is reported rather than replaced. The native descriptor preserves the cwd, preset, model route and narrow Project admission policy on cold continuation. The native Team Lead log owns membership, tasks and mailbox. Additive `team/control` records bind the Project host policy, cold capacity, cancelled messages, immutable assignment identities and explicit failed-member retry. No parallel worker execution engine is introduced.

Each delegation records its actual coordinator user-message and tool-call identity. A model request ID is not authorization. Runtime settlement may continue its original workstream within the original user scope, but cannot authorize unrelated work or restart a hold. Initial input uses an empty child seed.

The registered Lead/worker personas enforce the prompt contract at the model-instruction layer. Host briefs distinguish first assignment from continuation, retain the current delegation identity and scope, and supply the previous recorded report and prerequisite results. Follow-ups preserve correct earlier work; queued acceptance is distinct from actual execution. Prompt wording does not replace host permissions, cancellation or settlement checks.

The worker preset is stable across investigation, document work and development. Project roles explicitly use native tool presentation. The coordinator and read-only/document guards reject arbitrary `run_code` execution as well as shell and unrestricted filesystem tools. The effective scope and exact document paths are durable Project facts. Narrow `project_read`/`project_search` inspect the assigned directory; `project_write_document` writes only declared `.md`, `.mdx`, `.txt`, `.rst` and `.adoc` paths. Stage expansion within a saved requirement’s original authorization ceiling can follow a native settlement without a repeated user message. Expanding that ceiling requires a new actual human input and requirement revision. Effective stage scope changes only after the worker consumes its new brief. A busy expansion first interrupts and drains the prior activation, then continues the same Session. Native sandbox and delegated permissions remain authoritative.

Normal development uses the selected existing directory. Project workers serialize writes to overlapping canonical directories, including parent/child directories across Projects, until the previous worker and its owned Jobs stop. Independent read-only work and disjoint sibling directories can run in parallel. An independent Git worktree is an explicit parallel-development arrangement, never the default; it remains fixed for that workstream and is not registered as an empty sidebar Workspace. The desktop bridge checks its actual branch/identity. Windows checkout enables Git long paths for that command only; it changes no repository or global setting. The user’s selected directory is never reset or deleted.

An accepted development stage within its saved human requirement can enable native single-command approval when the Lead permits asking, including a stage following native settlement without another human turn. The exact worker command, working directory and work title appear in the Lead's normal approval composer. Allow once is limited to that pending command; reject and Stop withdraw it. Explicit `never` policy, read-only/document scope, standing sandbox permissions and ordinary Team defaults remain authoritative. Execution captures the consumed assignment's lifetime and checks it immediately before process creation, so a late grant cannot restart stopped work.

## Results and lifecycle

`project_report` records `completed`, `blocked` or `failed`, with a summary, real artifact references, evidence and explicit remaining issues. It then concludes the worker turn. A report alone does not complete the workstream: its delegation must match the current consumed request and the actual native terminal event. `done` means the worker reported completion and settled normally; it is not an independent verification claim. Idle without a report, an interrupted turn, missing input and failures remain blocked.

The native settled notice is the sole proactive worker-to-coordinator notification. `subagent/end` persists its run identity and updates notes. The coordinator’s existing pre-step hook waits for the matching bookkeeping barrier, then adds that run’s recorded reports, artifacts, evidence and remaining issues to the same native message. This covers workers that finish through `project_report` without a closing prose message. Message identity, native source and the single wake remain intact. An old run’s report never replaces a newer delegation’s status or grants new authority. Paused/stopped admission rejects automatic wakeups. Domain facts survive even when an Agent inbox is discarded on disposal; recovery reads them and does not publish synthetic replacement notices. `project_deliver` freezes the requirement version, necessary work and exact report/native run references. A draft commits only after a genuine visible Lead reply, completed turn and confirmed persistent Session flush, with version and evidence rechecked. Reading notes or replying with progress does not clear pending results. Duplicate declarations and failed flushes retain their exact original reply for restart reconciliation; recovery starts no worker. This is not a user-read receipt.

Stop first establishes its in-memory hold and real user-message cutoff and cancels owned work; failed persistence or notes cannot prevent cancellation or permit the same request to restart. The durable hold preserves the cutoff across recovery. The existing main composer Cancel hook and natural-language `project_stop` use the same Project stop path. An old coordinator turn cannot delegate itself out of that hold; a genuinely new user message is required. Workers and their owned Jobs drain; uncertain teardown stays `stopping` with a diagnostic and keeps directory occupancy. External user processes are never killed. Restart marks interrupted activity honestly and starts no model. Resume/restore only makes the Project available for a new user message. Archive retains all user directories, Session logs and Project materials.

The existing CLI shutdown owner drains Project before closing the Host storage tree. Bare Fiber unload performs runtime cancellation only, since Cordis releases facilities concurrently. After interruption, ordinary `turn/end` and a worker report do not prove the entire activation settled; recovery preserves these as blocked pending facts. Only a persisted native settlement establishes completion. Windows force termination is not a graceful-shutdown guarantee.

The `whale_project_local` storage domain stores projects, workstreams, workers, finite delegation/settlement receipts and optional Request/Delivery records. The abandoned Team experiment’s `whale_project` domain remains untouched and is never silently migrated. Session logs are the actual conversation history; notes are a readable projection. Project startup errors produce an unavailable Project service while ordinary Harness conversations remain available.

## Materials and UI

```text
$DSH_HOME/projects/<projectId>/
  notes.md
  preferences.md
  docs/<workstreamId>/
  internal/<workstreamId>/
```

The generated notes section precedes `<!-- whale-project:user-notes -->`; user prose below it is preserved. Preferences are assembled only in the coordinator scope and included in worker briefs, with current user instructions taking precedence. Deliverables are written as new files so earlier results remain available. Private work notes live outside the repository.

`project_read_store` permits notes, preferences, docs and bounded requirement/version/input reads. Worker material writes stay within its own docs/internal roots. Desktop material opening authorizes only this Project’s docs; reported repository artifacts must match their workstream’s fixed authorized directory. Realpath checks reject directory-link escapes.

The client registers its entry only when the Host reports availability. The sidebar has one row per coordinator. Progress uses the same TaskDock as ordinary conversation tasks, initially one line above the composer and expandable to bounded scrolling detail. Projects with no accepted requirement show a short instruction. A requirement with no worker still shows its goal, version and pending delivery. Work rows prioritize actual state and result/stop/retry actions; member history and file changes are in details, with directory, branch and consumed scope disclosed separately. Stopping precedes stopped until actual drain. Rename/archive/restore belong to the Project row context menu; an active archive drains owned work. The category menu exposes archived projects. Archive replaces the composer with a status notice; archived projects offer Restore there and protect notes/preferences editing. The shared Team action defaults to current members and recent work, pages historical native tasks and their original members, distinguishes idle from never-started work and opens the original worker history. Materials use Results, Notes and Project instructions tabs. Committed user deliveries show conclusion, requirement version, evidence and files before supporting member reports; a progress result targets that exact work, independently of results pagination. Earlier-report counts omit the displayed report. All saved documents are initially collapsed. File menus expose original locations without replacing recorded authority. Unsaved tab changes offer save/discard/keep editing, and save failure stays in the current confirmation with the draft intact. Worker history retains the original parent/child Session event source and has no second prompt. Task forms, manual dispatch, acceptance and member administration are absent.

Detail reads return at most 20 current work summaries and three recent historical summaries. Full execution/report data is read only when opening one work. Current work and history use replacement pages, retain the chosen page during polling and reject stale responses. Expanded history follows live revisions without losing its open state; a resumed history anchor explicitly returns to the first historical page. Deliveries and member reports have independent ten-item page cursors. Materials remain mounted when opening execution records, preserving the original page, disclosure and notes draft on return. Old deliveries and report history open their exact original assignment message in the same Session, loading older pages when needed; execution turn boundaries remain visible. Aggregate status describes the entire Project, including preparation and pending summaries, rather than only the visible page.

Queued work identifies the actual prerequisite, directory occupancy or native capacity holding it. Dependency admission checks the current completed receipt and native task together before freezing the supplied prerequisite references; preparation does not read a newer unfinished request as a completed result. Reports retain the references actually consumed by the member. A changed upstream request or replacement report marks the result as having changed prerequisites without rewriting history or restarting completed work.

Only an explicit committed Delivery consumes its precise report and native terminal references. A real summary error preserves the result and records the matching Session turn and report or terminal identity. The retry action sends a normal user message to that Lead; it does not replace the draft or dispatch worker work. Historical reports and outcomes without reports remain reachable in ten-item pages. Generated notes prioritize current blocked and active work and reserve a UTF-8 byte budget for the complete legal user notes suffix.

Public authenticated RPCs under `/dsh-project` are `list`, `create`, `detail`, `workstreams/list`, `workstreams/get`, `requirements/list`, `requirements/get`, `rename`, `stop`, `pause`, `resume`, `archive`, `restore`, `store/list`, `store/results`, `store/read`, `store/write`, `open` and `diff`. Delegation/reporting are scoped model tools and are not public workbench commands. The desktop patch mounts this plugin and native Team UI. Project reuses an existing Team service or composes one locally; it does not force-enable independent Team settings or edit user patch files.

## Validation boundary

Product implementation, focused Host checks, real provider conversation acceptance, visible desktop acceptance and packaged acceptance are separate evidence. Source or scripted-model checks alone do not certify a real-provider or installer path. This package changes no application version, publishing workflow or main branch.

The configured GPT-6.1-Sol · Codex route has exercised real continuing members, bidirectional peer collaboration with dependent document output, scoped development and local command execution, stop/restore and archive in isolated profiles. The default Node test runner has also passed on the original member through native allow-once approval, preserving the earlier sandbox failure in report history. Current source, packaged observations and installer identity are recorded in [the feature note](../../docs/features/projects.md). These observations do not authorize merging or publishing.

Selected Project directories provide desktop authority through their own durable canonical registrations, without empty ordinary Workspace rows. Creation validates the selected local directory; file/Git/process actions still require the persisted registration. Continuations synchronize the native task description, preserve the original member and only complete after its matching report, settlement and owned Jobs have drained. Peer messages remain bound to both active assignments.
